Figure 1:ScaleVLA overview.Top left: backbone sizes. Top right: the VLM encodes images and the instruction, and the action DiT uses these features and robot state to generate an action chunk.
Middle: task success by backbone size. Base is the best dense backbone at or below each size.
Bottom: inference latency on RoboCasa, sample efficiency on LIBERO Goal, and success on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO.

Figure 2:ScaleVLA architecture.The VLM encodes the images and the instruction, and the action head reads the output of its causal encoder.
The action DiT alternates cross-attention and self-attention and generates an action chunk in four flow steps.

Figure 3:Simulation tasks.LIBERO tests tabletop manipulation, LIBERO-PRO perturbs the objects and scenes of LIBERO, RoboCasa tests kitchen tasks in out-of-distribution scenes, and DexJoCo tests five tasks that require coordinating two dexterous hands.

Figure 5:Plug In Charger on a real robot.Left: all three policies grasp and hand over the charger from in-domain layouts. ScaleVLA aligns and inserts the plug; the other two policies reach the socket but fail to insert the plug.
Right: success rates in the in-domain and OOD settings.
